description: The platform threat model (P09.01): boundaries taken from diagrams/sources/05-security-trust-boundaries.mmd and the baseline's required areas, the assets worth protecting, and threats with their treatments. Risk is scored from likelihood and impact; safety impact is scored separately from information-security impact. The verifier computes each threat's status and residual risk from the state of its controls - a planned control earns no credit - so this file states the threats and the treatments and never the outcome.

scales.control_credit: Each implemented treating control lowers likelihood by one step, at most two steps. A partial or planned control lowers nothing.

boundaries.name: Devices and sensors
boundaries.description: Simulated loop detectors, signal controllers, weather, road-condition, pedestrian and cycle sensors, and the AVL units of emergency vehicles; in a real deployment, roadside equipment.

boundaries.name: Edge runtime and local models
boundaries.description: The edge container that validates, extracts features, runs the ONNX model or baseline, and keeps a durable outbox; no camera frame leaves it.

boundaries.name: MQTT broker and gateway
boundaries.description: The mTLS MQTT listener with per-device identity and topic ACLs, and the gateway that validates events and forwards them to the stream.

boundaries.name: Event backbone and ingestion
boundaries.description: The Kafka-compatible stream and the consumer that validates and persists observations exactly once by meaning.

boundaries.name: Data stores and audit evidence
boundaries.description: PostgreSQL/PostGIS records (topology, telemetry, incidents, commands, outcomes, calls) and the append-only audit and history tables.

boundaries.name: Staff API and live feed
boundaries.description: The FastAPI service that answers the operator console: REST, WebSocket, authorization, workflow endpoints and the governance endpoints.

boundaries.name: Operator web application
boundaries.description: The browser console: sign-in, live map, dispatch, approvals, audit, platform status.

boundaries.name: Identity provider
boundaries.description: Keycloak: realm, roles, demo identities, the browser client and the service clients.

boundaries.name: Policy decision point
boundaries.description: The execution-time command policy today and Open Policy Agent (P09.03): who may do what to which target, now.

boundaries.name: Command path and controller adapters
boundaries.description: Request, approval, the executor worker, the verifier worker and the simulator signal, diversion and sign adapters.

boundaries.name: Models and datasets
boundaries.description: Training data, evaluation ledgers, ONNX artifacts, forecast and detector packages.

boundaries.name: Build, dependencies and images
boundaries.description: Source repository, Python and Node dependencies, base images, CI workflows and release artifacts.

boundaries.name: Human operators and administrators
boundaries.description: The people behind the roles: operators, supervisors, dispatchers, incident commanders, auditors, field responders and platform administrators.

boundaries.name: External integrations
boundaries.description: CAD/AVL feeds, public-warning channels, transit and V2X feeds. All simulated today; none is authorized as a real connection.

boundaries.name: Demo and scenario control
boundaries.description: The separate scenario-control service and the demo operator identity.

boundaries.name: Cluster and host runtime
boundaries.description: Kubernetes or Docker hosts, container runtime, network and secrets storage (Phase 11).

boundaries.name: Observability pipeline
boundaries.description: Logs, metrics and traces and their storage and dashboards (Phase 10).

assets.name: Safe operation of signals and the road-user safety it protects
Emergency call and unit data (no patient or medical data is held)
Availability of the platform and its identity, policy and data services
Source, dependencies, images and release artifacts
The truthfulness of what an operator sees (freshness, source, identity)

threats.title: A device is impersonated to inject false readings
threats.description: An attacker presents another detector's identity or invents a device to report counts, phases or positions that are not real.

threats.title: Captured telemetry is replayed
threats.description: Recorded valid events are sent again to make a road look quiet or busy, or to bury a real reading.

threats.title: A device is stolen or opened and its key extracted
threats.description: Physical access to roadside equipment yields the device's private key, which then authenticates as that device.

threats.title: Camera-derived data or tracks identify individuals
threats.description: Vehicle or pedestrian tracks, plates or faces, if kept or sent, single out identifiable people.

threats.title: A faulty or compromised device floods the platform
threats.description: One device sends events far above its normal rate and crowds out the rest.

threats.title: A tampered model is activated at an edge site
threats.description: An unverified or substituted model artifact changes detections at the edge.

threats.title: The edge outbox is altered on disk
threats.description: Buffered events are removed or forged while the site is offline.

threats.title: The edge loses the network, identity or central services
threats.description: An intersection keeps running while cut off; telemetry piles up and central views go stale.

threats.title: Raw camera frames or intermediate data are retained locally
threats.description: Frames or features are kept longer than needed or copied off the device.

threats.title: A device publishes under another device's identity or topic
threats.description: A valid client certificate is used to publish on a topic that belongs to a different device.

threats.title: A client subscribes to other devices' topics
threats.description: A wildcard or guessed topic lets a device read telemetry or commands meant for others.

threats.title: The broker or gateway is flooded or a consumer stalls
threats.description: Publishing faster than the gateway or stream can absorb loses or delays events.

threats.title: A certificate from an untrusted authority is accepted
threats.description: A rogue or self-signed certificate authenticates a device.

threats.title: A poisoned or conflicting event overwrites a stored observation
threats.description: An event reusing an existing identifier with different content replaces the original record.

threats.title: Redelivery duplicates or reorders events
threats.description: At-least-once delivery produces duplicate rows or out-of-order state that later cannot be explained.

threats.title: An unauthorized consumer reads the stream
threats.description: The stream carries every device's telemetry and is reachable inside the platform network without transport protection or ACLs.

threats.title: Ingestion lag hides fresh data behind old data
threats.description: A backlog makes central state older than it looks.

threats.title: Audit or history rows are rewritten to hide an action
threats.description: Someone with database rights changes or deletes evidence of a command, approval or refusal.

threats.title: A person denies having requested, approved or denied a command
threats.description: Without a reliable record of who did what in which role, accountability is lost.

threats.title: Database credentials are read from configuration or the process environment
threats.description: The shared application password is used to read or change any table.

threats.title: Audit details or exports carry tokens, identifiers or locations
threats.description: Free-text or structured detail written to audit records exposes secrets or personal data to whoever can read them.

threats.title: SQL injection through an API parameter
threats.description: A crafted filter, cursor or identifier reaches a query as code.

threats.title: Data is lost with no restorable backup
threats.description: A storage failure or destructive change cannot be recovered from.

threats.title: Location or trajectory data is kept beyond its purpose
threats.description: Retention that never expires turns operational data into a movement history.

threats.title: A forged, expired or wrong-audience token is accepted
threats.description: A token signed with the wrong key, minted for another client, or past its lifetime reaches a protected endpoint.

threats.title: A role calls a capability it does not hold
threats.description: An operator, field responder or demo operator reaches an approval, dispatch or audit endpoint.

threats.title: A user of one agency reads or changes another agency's records
threats.description: Roles are global; call and unit data carry an agency scope that the API does not yet enforce per user.
threats.accepted: This prototype is one operating organisation: emergency-service collaboration is modelled as handover messages (P07.03), not as separate user populations, so no user can belong to a different agency. It becomes a real gap the day a second agency signs in.

threats.title: Responses carry more than the caller needs
threats.description: Internal addresses, identifiers or stack traces reach roles that do not need them.

threats.title: A request flood or oversized body exhausts the API
threats.description: An authenticated client, or many, overwhelms the service or its database connections.

threats.title: Mass assignment: a client names its own author, requester or status
threats.description: A request body supplies fields the server must decide (author, requester, role, status).

threats.title: The access token in the WebSocket URL is logged or cached
threats.description: A browser cannot set headers on a WebSocket, so the short-lived token rides in the query string, where proxies and logs may keep it.
threats.accepted: Tokens live 300 s and are audience-bound; the alternative (a ticket endpoint) is recorded as a design option for P11 when a real reverse proxy exists.

threats.title: A new endpoint ships without an authorization decision
threats.description: A developer adds a route and forgets the policy entry.

threats.title: Cross-site scripting steals or misuses the session
threats.description: Injected script reads the access token or acts as the operator.

threats.title: The console is framed or spoofed by another origin
threats.description: Clickjacking or a look-alike page tricks an operator into approving.

threats.title: The screen shows old or cached data as if it were live
threats.description: An operator acts on a picture that is minutes old without knowing.

threats.title: Phishing or an open redirect during sign-in
threats.description: The person is sent to a look-alike identity page or the code is delivered to another origin.

threats.title: A demonstration screen or simulated data is mistaken for real operations
threats.description: The demo identity or the simulated feed is read as a live city.

threats.title: Passwords are guessed or stuffed against operator accounts
threats.description: Repeated attempts try to take over a role.

threats.title: A client or redirect misconfiguration leaks tokens or codes
threats.description: A wildcard redirect, implicit grant or missing PKCE lets an attacker capture a token.

threats.title: The identity provider is down when tokens expire
threats.description: Nobody can sign in or renew; the console cannot tell an ended session from an outage.

threats.title: The realm drifts from the reviewed configuration
threats.description: A setting is loosened in the running realm and the file in Git no longer describes it.

threats.title: The administrator console or its credentials are exposed
threats.description: Whoever holds them can create users and roles.

threats.title: A protected action skips the policy decision
threats.description: A code path, worker or endpoint performs an action without asking.

threats.title: The policy engine fails open
threats.description: When the decision point is down, a high-impact command is approved anyway.

threats.title: The policy rules or their data are altered
threats.description: A changed rule or role table silently widens what is allowed.

threats.title: A command is aimed at a target it was not approved for
threats.description: The target entity, adapter or parameters change between approval and execution.

threats.title: A requester approves their own command, or two low roles collude
threats.description: Separation of duties is bypassed for a high-class action.

threats.title: An old approved command is replayed
threats.description: A command that was valid once is executed again later or twice.

threats.title: A signal change creates an unsafe state
threats.description: A phase change shortens pedestrian clearance or produces conflicting greens.

threats.title: An action makes things worse and is not undone
threats.description: A closure or timing change worsens traffic and stays in place.

threats.title: A person or another service reaches an adapter
threats.description: Anything other than the executor identity calls a signal, sign or diversion adapter.

threats.title: The adapter is unreachable or does not acknowledge
threats.description: The controller's real state becomes unknown after a command.

threats.title: Training data is poisoned or leaks into evaluation
threats.description: Manipulated or overlapping data inflates a detector's or forecaster's apparent quality.

threats.title: A model drifts or is fooled by unusual input
threats.description: Accuracy degrades in operation without anyone noticing.

threats.title: Service quality is unequal across areas or road users
threats.description: A detector or forecast performs worse for some roads, modes or scenarios.

threats.title: Operators over-rely on a recommendation
threats.description: A ranked suggestion is accepted without weighing its harm or uncertainty (automation bias).

threats.title: A malicious or vulnerable dependency is installed
threats.description: A compromised package or a known-vulnerable version enters the build.

threats.title: A tampered image or artifact is deployed
threats.description: An image differs from what was built and reviewed.

threats.title: A secret is committed or a CI token is abused
threats.description: A credential in history or a broad token lets someone act as the project.

threats.title: An insider approves harmful commands
threats.description: Coercion, fatigue or malice leads a legitimate approver to approve something unsafe.

threats.title: An override is used without a record
threats.description: A commander bypasses a gate and nothing shows it.

threats.title: Accounts keep roles they no longer need
threats.description: A person who changed job or left still holds an operating role.

threats.title: A forged CAD or AVL feed creates false calls or moves units
threats.description: An outside feed is trusted without authentication.
threats.accepted: No real CAD/AVL integration is authorized or connected; the prototype's feeds are simulated and labelled as such. Any real adapter needs its own authenticated, tested integration before this risk applies.

threats.title: A false public warning is sent through a notification channel
threats.description: A message reaches the public that no one approved.
threats.accepted: No public-warning adapter exists; nothing can be sent to the public. Building one would need its own threat review.

threats.title: An integration credential leaks
threats.description: A key for an external system is committed or logged.

threats.title: Demo controls reach the operational command path
threats.description: A demonstration action changes real incidents, commands or devices.

threats.title: Demo activity is mixed into the operational audit trail
threats.description: Evidence of real actions is diluted or confused with demonstrations.

threats.title: A wrong or runaway remediation worsens an outage
threats.description: An automatic restart, failover or scale action makes a platform incident larger.

threats.title: The remediation identity is used to reach traffic actions
threats.description: A service allowed to restart platform parts is used to change signals.

threats.title: A container escape or over-privileged workload
threats.description: A compromised service breaks out or holds rights it does not need.

threats.title: Lateral movement between services
threats.description: A compromised component reaches databases or adapters it should not.

threats.title: Secrets are readable from cluster or host state
threats.description: Keys and passwords sit in manifests, environment or storage that many can read.

threats.title: Malicious runtime behaviour goes unnoticed
threats.description: A shell in a container, a read of a sensitive file or a write to a binary directory produces no alert.

threats.title: Resource exhaustion starves safety-critical services
threats.description: A noisy workload takes the memory, disk or CPU that identity, policy or the command path need.

threats.title: Logs, metrics or traces contain tokens or personal identifiers
threats.description: Telemetry about the platform leaks what the platform protects.

threats.title: Telemetry is poisoned to mislead operators or AIOps
threats.description: Forged health or metrics make a fault look fine or a fine system look faulty.
